## 2. Exact upstream source and build boundary

Use **official Rust BLAKE3 1.8.7** with its `wasm32_simd` feature, never a custom compression/tree implementation or an assumed C SIMD backend. Immutable upstream revision is `f3149ec5bb5449af877ba20377a11008ff499fa2` at tag 1.8.7. Exact official crate archive is `https://static.crates.io/crates/blake3/blake3-1.8.7.crate`, 209,726 bytes, SHA-256 `6d9e454fc11f76977dc803893aff6304ed33d6a26efae8696573bea74baa27ae`. Its `.cargo_vcs_info.json` identifies that revision; scoped inspection confirmed its `src/lib.rs`, `src/platform.rs`, `src/wasm32_simd.rs`, `build.rs` and three licenses byte-match the immutable GitHub source. Keep this source unmodified. Version 1.8.7 also removes the arrayref dependency after the upstream owner compromise; do not substitute an older source for convenience.

Primary references: [official release](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/releases/tag/1.8.7), [pinned Cargo features](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/blob/f3149ec5bb5449af877ba20377a11008ff499fa2/Cargo.toml), [public incremental implementation](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/blob/f3149ec5bb5449af877ba20377a11008ff499fa2/src/lib.rs), [platform dispatch](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/blob/f3149ec5bb5449af877ba20377a11008ff499fa2/src/platform.rs), and [four-lane Wasm backend](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/blob/f3149ec5bb5449af877ba20377a11008ff499fa2/src/wasm32_simd.rs). The source path is `Hasher::update` → `update_with_join<SerialJoin>` → subtree/chunk compression → `Platform::hash_many` → `wasm32_simd::hash_many` → `hash4` for complete four-chunk batches. SIMD degree is four. Upstream assumes feature support, so the adapter must select before consuming input.

Add a private native build under `native/blake3/`: a small `no_std` Rust `cdylib` wrapper depending on exact `blake3 = "=1.8.7"`, `default-features = false`, `features = ["wasm32_simd"]`; a wrapper-owned Cargo.lock; pinned rust-toolchain; and unmodified source vendored with Cargo's standard locked source-replacement mechanism. Vendor the resolved build/runtime crates with their checksum metadata, contents and licenses intact. Do not add the upstream repository's development workspace or optional ecosystems outside that resolved wrapper graph. The package remains adapter-owned; no separate npm package, runtime Cargo, wasm-bindgen, WASI, allocator, threading, Rayon, Rust std, or additional npm crypto dependency.

Available toolchain: rustc 1.97.1, commit `8bab26f4f68e0e26f0bb7960be334d5b520ea452`; cargo 1.97.1; target `wasm32-unknown-unknown` installed. Pin/verify the exact rustc verbose identity, Cargo identity and target in the build. Use Rust's bundled linker, release optimization/LTO, panic abort, explicit `+simd128`, explicit bounded stack and initial/max memory. Freeze actual final flags and tool identities in the manifest rather than guessing artifact hashes now. Do not add wasm-opt unless an evidenced need appears; the existing SHA256 Emscripten build remains unchanged.

Follow the existing `scripts/build-sha256-wasm.mjs` pattern with a small BLAKE3 build script: intentional `--update` writes generated inline Wasm TypeScript plus a manifest; `--verify` rebuilds cleanly and compares exact bytes, source/toolchain/flags and manifest. Wire a `build:blake3:wasm` verification command into `npm run check`. Normal JS build, pack and consumer installation use checked-in generated bytes and require no Rust/network. Verify from two distinct clean build directories so paths/caches do not accidentally determine output. Normalize/remap paths as necessary; do not commit build caches or archive downloads.

Manifest records upstream tag/revision/archive checksum, wrapper and vendored-source/checksum identities, Cargo.lock and toolchain identities, full flags, Wasm SHA-256, imports/exports, stack/input/output/state layout information, and initial/maximum memory. Copy verbatim BLAKE3 licenses into packaged notices, preserve existing hash-wasm notices, identify all linked dependency/runtime license obligations from the actual build, and update NOTICE plus package copy/check scripts. Preserve original upstream copyright/provenance in vendored sources. This is a dependency attribution task, not a new licensing policy.

## 3. Minimal ABI, ownership and memory contract

Keep the asynchronous `createIncrementalBlake3()` contract and existing stream/store/worker callers. Compile immutable SIMD code once per realm with a single-flight promise. Each factory call instantiates its own **nonshared fixed memory, one upstream Hasher, one 16 KiB staging area and one 32-byte result area**. No instance/state pool, arena allocator, saved-state copies, handles, cross-worker sharing or permanent cached mutable instance. A module-global Rust state is operation-owned because the entire module instance is operation-owned.

The narrow internal ABI exports memory, fixed input/result address accessors (and input capacity if useful), initialization/reset, bounded update length, and finalize-to-32-bytes. Call only public upstream `Hasher::new`/`reset`, `update` and `finalize`; do not expose keyed hashing, XOF, hazmat/CV internals or create algorithm glue. Use distinct properly aligned storage and valid nonaliasing Rust borrows; never create references to uninitialized Hasher memory. Validate lengths before constructing Rust slices. Oversized/invalid ABI inputs must trap or return an explicit failure before memory/state corruption. No host callbacks/imports means synchronous operations cannot reenter the Rust state. Keep export names/layout private and check exact module shape in the build.

Start with **128 KiB fixed initial=max linear memory**, a conservative explicit stack (64 KiB is a reasonable first choice), 16 KiB staging and fixed Hasher/result storage. A measured build may use up to **256 KiB fixed memory** if needed for justified linker/stack space; record the actual layout and remaining lane headroom. This is an allowed bounded implementation choice, not a promise that 128 KiB already works. If more than 256 KiB or memory growth is needed, stop this attempt for scope review rather than expanding reservations. Require no `memory.grow`, allocator/free ABI or dynamic native allocations in init/update/finalize, stable memory buffer/length over long representative streams, and failed external growth on a sacrificial instance. Static declaration is not a physical-memory measurement or a proof that successive completed states have already been reclaimed.

Retain the current 2 MiB per-warm-lane reservation: 512 KiB payload + 64 KiB zero scratch + <=256 KiB packed metadata + <=256 KiB BLAKE3 memory + existing 64 KiB control allowance leaves >=896 KiB headroom. Keep three workers, current cold funding and app +6 MiB unchanged. Fresh completed operation instances remain subject to GC just as today; prove retention with matched measurements. Dropping operation references and existing worker termination is the cleanup model. No new destroy protocol or call-site finalizer churn is needed for allocation-free instance-owned state.

Updates synchronously copy through reusable staging and call upstream update with up to 16 KiB, preserving current bridge size and enough chunks for four-lane work. Reuse the memory view; do not retain input, allocate a payload-sized copy, grow memory, add a Promise/yield per bridge block, or change existing read/zero checkpoint boundaries. Small non-owning subarray views are acceptable where normal typed-array copy needs them; do not replace a bulk copy with a slow handwritten byte loop to claim zero allocations. Output allocation once at finalization is expected.

Preserve initialized factory state; chainable init/update; default/explicit lowercase 64-character hex; binary output as an independent 32-byte copy; digest invalidating the operation; repeat digest/update after digest rejecting until init; and reset/output lifetime. Audit existing internal consumers and preserve their Uint8Array/offset semantics. Prefer preserving currently accepted typed-array/string inputs at the private wrapper edge; do not accidentally expose hash-wasm's unrelated save/load methods through return typing. No public package API or session/hash format changes.

## 4. Backend selection and preserved verifier authority

Use the existing pinned hash-wasm 4.12.0 as the scalar compatibility fallback. It stays an exact dependency with its license and independent test oracle. Detect compatibility by validating the actual embedded SIMD module once per realm before instantiation; a `false` result selects scalar before any bytes are consumed. This also catches unsupported Wasm features emitted by the pinned target. No eager scalar instance is created on a successful SIMD path.

Unexpected validation exceptions, failure to compile an otherwise validated artifact, malformed exports/memory, initialization failure, update failure or digest failure must reject the operation. Never silently retry a partially consumed stream or hide a valid-module failure as a scalar success. Clear a rejected in-flight compile promise so a later independent operation can retry; do not permanently cache a rejected mutable result. Existing lack-of-WebAssembly behavior remains unchanged. Add no public backend override or production diagnostic framework; focused tests may force the support decision in a fresh realm/private test seam.

Preserve canonical BLAKE3-256 for every active byte and every leading/interior/trailing zero gap in exact timeline order. Preserve 512 KiB interval-local reads and returned-buffer disposal; 64 KiB zero updates/yields; source order; admitted metadata; byte/read/update/digest/identity checks; deadlines and watchdogs; bounded progress/ACK/backpressure; cancellation and stale-generation rejection; failure mapping; worker teardown/claim/lock ordering; and failure-before-ready. A dispatch/init fault never permits worker success or aggregate ready. Existing dense FLAC hashing and local/main-realm fallback use the same wrapper and need their current regression gates.

Excluded: engine, audio, codec, decode/transport SHA256, pump, cache/backend changes, new workers, read-ahead, read size, zero size, source concurrency, scheduling/funding, session format/algorithm, whole-stem buffering and product UI. A package-version bump/publication/app registry adoption is Root-owned after qualification, not an implementation prerequisite.

## 5. Compact correctness and actual delivery gates

Extend `tests/blake3.test.ts` and the existing relevant worker/store fixtures; do not build a Cartesian matrix or duplicate every existing cancellation test.

1. Use the official pinned test-vector file with its deterministic `input[i] = i % 251` rule. Retain empty/abc vectors and a compact multi-chunk subset (including 1024, 4096 and a larger tree boundary), comparing the first 32 expected bytes. Source vector SHA-256 is `dcb91ea8accc77e6d6e632af7cdc1a99a9f3ae78cf648da595c7d064db32f624` at the pinned commit. Freeze only the needed fixtures/expected values with provenance.
2. Differential against independent hash-wasm for lengths around 64, 1024, 4096, **16384 staging**, 65536 and 524288 bytes, including minus/at/plus-one boundaries. Assign varied streaming splits across these cases; include empty updates, nonzero-offset views and a partial last block. One 37,247,538-byte bounded synthetic stream covers repeated large updates without allocating the full input.
3. Interleave two differently valued, differently split hash states across awaits and reset/finalize operations; verify independent outputs. Test binary output survives reset/other operations, terminal-use errors and invalid input. Do not use identical A/B streams as the only independence oracle.
4. One active/zero/active sparse canonical fixture has leading/interior/trailing zeros, multiple reads and a partial tail. Independently compare full canonical bytes/digest. Reuse existing tamper, byte-count, zero-order, short-read, deadline, cancellation, detached-read, failure-before-ready and actual worker teardown cases. Existing success fixtures must use the new selected backend.
5. In fresh realms, verify unsupported-module selection runs the real scalar fallback and matches vectors/splits. Verify a validated-module compile/init failure rejects before input consumption/readiness; update/digest faults do not switch backend. Exercise concurrent first creation so immutable compilation is shared while mutable instances stay independent.
6. Decode/disassemble the **exact generated and packed worker artifact bytes**. Record SHA-256, imports/exports, fixed memory and actual SIMD instructions; establish the reachable incremental update → four-lane hash-many path from the pinned source/build plus artifact call graph (account for inlining). An unused vector function, one-shot-only entry or filename claiming SIMD does not pass. Check stable memory through boundary/long/interleaved tests and absence of native growth/allocation paths. Do not add permanent runtime tracing just for this evidence.

Run focused tests, then `npm run check` including the reproducible native build, packed fresh-consumer `npm run test:browser`, the existing indexed-sparse three-worker lane, and relevant actual OPFS success/reopen/teardown. Require real packed Chromium and existing macOS Chromium/WebKit qualification before release; source imports, Node-only tests or Linux WebKit fallback cannot replace that evidence. Exercise the forced scalar-support decision with real packed browser bytes in a fresh worker/test entry as well as the supported SIMD path. Reuse/extend existing harnesses and CI rather than adding a general browser/crypto framework. Preserve exact engine 0.2.4 and codec 0.1.1 artifact hashes. Package checks verify included inline bytes and licenses, no runtime fetch/compiler/new crypto package, and no leaked native build/cache files.

Fresh non-implementing Astra medium reviews the frozen diff, unsafe ABI/state ownership, official source/lock/toolchain/license pins, actual four-lane reachability, fallback/failure semantics, test oracles and exact package/browser evidence. Findings must be corrected and rechecked; implementation author's passing tests are not an independent verdict.

## 6. Fixed performance qualification and stop rules

Use one candidate only. Root records source revisions/dirty patches, archive/dist hashes, current registry control identity, app/harness/analyzer/config identities, browser/device and immutable engine/codec identities. Both arms use three warm workers, identical app policy/source order/authenticated Ghost preference 8, cold cache fill, one unmeasured warm prime, and fresh navigation through `about:blank`. Hash module startup/compile belongs inside each fresh load; no worker prewarming. Existing scalar observation may retain bounded counts/digests only, never payloads or detailed timelines.

**Memory before speed claims:** after correctness/packed proof/review, run exactly three AB/BA/AB pairs using the existing combined main-plus-attributable-dedicated-worker collector. Include before/peak/teardown/matched-reopen state, all worker contributions, actual counts and incomplete-sample coverage. Pass only if `median(candidate combined peaks) - median(control combined peaks) <= 8,388,608 bytes`, with complete target attribution, no unexplained retained growth, increasing worker count or failed cleanup. Preserve unknown transition samples and disclose unmeasured browser/native/OPFS memory. Main-only sampling or declared Wasm pages cannot pass this gate. Failure/missing coverage stops timing.

**Hash-only proof after memory passes:** reuse `/tmp/miso-hash-comparison/` and the existing report's bounded deterministic worker harness with current scalar and the exact packed embedded wrapper. One warmup, five paired alternating-order 37,247,538-byte streams at 512 KiB caller updates, plus the existing 64 KiB zero case; record every create/update+digest/startup measurement and independent digest. Keep the existing fixed three-worker/eight-job check; no concurrency sweep. Fresh-worker compile/initialization is reported separately. The large-stream median should improve to support the hashing optimization claim; the short timer-sensitive zero case is diagnostic. If SIMD loses on the representative stream, record/review the failure and stop this candidate rather than tune buffer sizes or swap implementations. Published awasm numbers are context, not the control.

**App readiness after memory and hash pass:** exactly five timing-only AB/BA/AB/BA/AB pairs. Every warm row must verify eight distinct identities and full digests, zero stem network requests, exactly 845 reads, 249,323,400 active/read bytes, 297,980,304 canonical/hashed bytes, 1,010 zero updates, three native verification workers and complete teardown, with no fallback or protocol/page errors. Let paired saving `d_i = controlReady_i - candidateReady_i`; require at least four positive pairs and `median(d) > max(10 ms, 0.01 * median(controlReady), 2 * MAD(d))`. Do not substitute summed overlapping hash service for readiness savings. No extra pairs, discarded unfavorable rows, extra variants or tuned scheduling.

Retain the separate existing Ghost responsiveness pair: heartbeat p95 increase <=10 ms, no new verifier-attributable main task >50 ms, committed-progress gap <=250 ms while bytes advance. Existing external CPU/withheld-read cancellation and fairness checks remain intact; run the available compact gates without expanding to a new matrix.

Only positive correctness, reproducibility, packing, browser, independent review, memory, hash, responsiveness and app-readiness evidence supports release/adoption. Otherwise archive this one candidate and retain current release. Root owns issue synchronization, exact candidate app installation for measurement and any later approved publication/exact registry adoption. Tracked app adoption additionally requires `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run build` and unchanged engine/codec provenance.

Detailed implementation/review and retained logs use the paths in section 7.
